carrier_or_model: Markov Coarse-Graining Benchmark: We begin with the controlled finite-state benchmark in which the exact object CD_tau(Pi) is available by construction. The benchmark consists of four families: exactly lumpable chains , perturbed-lumpable chains with heterogeneity parameter alpha ∈ \ 0,0.2,0.5\ , metastable block chains with escape parameter p_ out ∈ \ 0.02,0.08,0.20\ , and hidden-type chains with within-fiber type strength in \ 0.1,0.5,0.9\ . Across these 17 staged conditions we compute the exact closure deficit, the intrinsic term, the decomposition residual, and both uniform- and stationary-lift route mismatch. The benchmark behaves exactly as predicts on the closed cases. The exactly lumpable constructions collapse to machine zero at both staging depths: at tau=1 , for example, the benchmark gives CD_1(Pi)=4.34× 10^ -17 and RM^ uniform _1(Pi)=5.29× 10^ -17 . The decomposition identity is numerically stable throughout the sweep, with maximum absolute residual 2.87× 10^ -16 over all rows. In this sense the benchmark serves as a calibration device: the exact object vanishes when it should vanish, and the numerical implementation does not introduce visible leakage.
